result.topic_en: Formula-only notes computing an integral of the type $\int e^{x^2/(4\pi i)+\beta x}/(e^x-1)\,dx$ (Riemann–Siegel type integral) by completing the square and shifting the path of integration by $2\pi i$.
result.transcription:
$\int \frac{e^{\frac{xx}{4\pi i}+\beta x}}{1-e^{x}}\partial x$

$e^{\frac{xx}{4\pi i}+(\beta+n)x}$

$\frac{1}{4\pi i}(x+(\beta+n)2\pi i)^2 - \pi i\, nn$

$Q=\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\frac{e^{\frac{xx}{4\pi i}+\beta x}}{e^{x}-1}\partial x \qquad x=y+2\pi i$

$=\int\frac{e^{\frac{yy}{4\pi i}+y+\beta y}}{e^{y}-1}\partial y\; e^{\pi i+2\beta\pi i}$

$Q(e^{-2\beta\pi i}+1)$

[upside down at bottom: illegible note in Kurrent]

methods.what: Completing the square in the exponent of the integrand term $e^{x^2/(4\pi i)+(\beta+n)x}$
Shift of integration path by $2\pi i$ in the integral Q, producing a factor $e^{\pi i+2\beta\pi i}$
methods.quote: $=\int\frac{e^{\frac{yy}{4\pi i}+y+\beta y}}{e^{y}-1}\partial y\; e^{\pi i+2\beta\pi i}$

methods.what: Definition of the integral Q over the real line
Resulting combination of Q with factor $(e^{-2\beta\pi i}+1)$
